google_flights.label: Google Flights
google_flights.what_it_does: Pre-filled one-way search for a single leg. Confirms the flight exists and shows a price.

kayak.label: Kayak
kayak.what_it_does: Pre-filled one-way search for a single leg.

NH.name: All Nippon Airways
NH.note: Multiple Stopover Service is booked through ANA's own multi-city flow; a stopover over 24h is where the free first stopover applies.

BR.name: EVA Air
BR.note: No published stopover programme, but multi-city pricing is often at or below the connecting fare — worth pricing directly here.

FI.name: Icelandair
FI.note: Its booking engine supports stopovers directly — no multi-city workaround needed.

TP.name: TAP Air Portugal
TP.note: Portugal Stopover can be added at purchase or later via Manage Booking.

multi_city_deeplink.verification: Opened in a browser against a real search: Google Flights loads in multi-city mode with both legs pre-filled and prices the pair as ONE ticket, including partner carriers offering the two segments together more cheaply. That is the product's core claim, confirmed end to end.
multi_city_deeplink.format: Google's tfs parameter — a base64url-encoded protobuf. Encoder in src/engine/tfs.mjs, written against the community-documented schema and verified by decoding its own output with an independent reader rather than by comparing it against itself.
multi_city_deeplink.known_fragility: Google does not PUBLISH this format, so it can change without notice. That is a reason to keep fallbacks and to say so on the card — it was briefly a reason not to build it at all, which was wrong: without it the app could find an itinerary and then only tell the user to go retype it.
fallbacks_retained: Per-leg Google Flights searches using the ordinary user-facing query format.
The carrier's own booking site, where a multi-city ticket is bought directly.
multi_city_deeplink.if_it_breaks: Symptom is a blank or single-leg Google Flights search. Re-check the schema, or fall back to the per-leg links, which use a stable format.
